title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Threatening LSO Complaints
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: During settlement negotiations, opposing counsel is being difficult and refusing to compromise. To force a favorable settlement, the paralegal threatens to report opposing counsel to the Law Society of Ontario for incompetence. Is this ethical?
options: Yes, if the paralegal genuinely believes opposing counsel is incompetent.
Yes, negotiations allow for aggressive leverage tactics.
No, a paralegal shall not threaten to report another licensee to the Law Society to secure a civil advantage.
No, complaints to the Law Society can only be made by the clients themselves.
questions.explain: Rule 2.02 (Honesty and Candour) explicitly states that a paralegal shall not claim, or threaten to claim, that another licensee has committed a professional offence in order to gain a civil advantage for a client.
